source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And when a vast crowd of people pressed around him — like one treading [or: trampling] in a winepress — he began to say to his disciples: Guard yourselves against the leaven [or: influence] of the Pharisees, which is deceit [or: fraud, hypocrisy].

translation_notes: וכאשר (אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight/happy', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because with prefixed כ and ו this forms 'and when', a temporal conjunction introducing the scene.

בגת (גת): Candidates: H1660 'wine-press', H1661 'Gath (city)'. Chose H1660 because the preceding word כדורך ('like one who treads') creates a coherent image of treading in a winepress, describing the crushing crowd — 'treading in Gath' makes less contextual sense.

לאמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the infinitive construct לאמר ('to say') following 'he began' is standard Hebrew narrative syntax.
textual_notes: התמרו — this appears to be a reflexive/hitpael form meaning 'guard/beware yourselves'. The root is not provided with Strong's candidates. It could relate to שמר (guard) or a denominative form. The context ('of the leaven of the Pharisees') clearly demands a warning verb.

מהכאת — parsed as מ (from) + הכאת. This word is not standard biblical Hebrew for 'leaven' (שאור). It may be a later Hebrew or dialectal form. The context (warning about the Pharisees' influence described as deceit) strongly suggests 'leaven' as the intended meaning.
כדורך — 'like one treading': the imagery of crowd pressure compared to treading in a winepress is unusual but vivid. The כ prefix is comparative.

verses.literal: And when [a] multitude [of] peoples surrounded him like [one who] treads in [a] winepress he began to say to his disciples beware of the leaven of the Pharisees which is deceit

verses.translation: Nothing is hidden that will not be revealed [or: uncovered]; there is no thing concealed that will not come to open disclosure.

translation_notes: דבר (first): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because this is the subject noun — 'a thing is not hidden' — producing a coherent proverb about concealment and revelation.

אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 because it functions as 'there is not' negating the existence of any covered thing that won't be disclosed.
דבר (second): Same reasoning as first — H1697 'a thing/matter'.
שלא (both): לא candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808; the ש prefix is the relative particle 'that', creating 'that not' = 'that will not'.

verses.literal: [A] thing is not hidden that not will be revealed no thing covered that not will come to disclosure

verses.translation: And those things that you spoke in [the] darkness will be declared [or: proclaimed] in the light, and what you whispered in [the] ear in secret [or: in intimate counsel] will be proclaimed from [a] high place.

translation_notes: בחשך (חשך): Candidates: H2820 'to restrain/spare', H2821 'to be dark', H2822 'the dark/darkness', H2823 'dark (obscure)'. Chose H2822 because with prefix ב ('in') it means 'in darkness', parallel to 'in light' in the second clause — producing a clear antithetical parallelism.

באור (אור): Candidates: H215 'to make luminous', H216 'illumination/light', H217 'flame/the East', H218 'Ur (place)'. Chose H216 because 'in light' is the natural antithesis of 'in darkness', completing the parallelism.
ומה (מה): Candidates: H4100 'what?/how?', H4101 same (Aramaic). Chose H4100 — 'and what' introduces the second parallel clause about what was spoken in the ear.
בסוד: H5475 'a session/intimacy/secret counsel'. Only candidate. Fits perfectly — whispering in the ear 'in secret/in intimate counsel'.

במקום: Candidates: H4725 'a standing/place/locality', H6965 'to rise', H6966 'to rise (Aramaic)'. Chose H4725 because ב + מקום = 'in a place', modified by גבוה 'high', producing 'in a high place' — i.e. proclaimed publicly from an elevated position.
textual_notes: נא1מרים — the numeral 1 appears to be a manuscript artifact or scribal mark within the word. Reading as נאמרים (niphal participle plural of אמר, 'being said/declared').

נדרש — niphal of דרש ('to seek/inquire'). In niphal it can mean 'sought out' or 'expounded/proclaimed'. Given the parallel structure (things said in darkness → said in light; things whispered → proclaimed on high), 'proclaimed' or 'demanded/required' fits best, though 'sought out' is also viable.

verses.literal: And those things that you said in darkness will be said in light and what you spoke in [the] ear in secret will be sought out in [a] place high

verses.translation: And I say to you, beloved [or: friends]: do not fear those who put to death the body, and after [that] have nothing else [or: no other thing] that they can do. Those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them — do you think that they were more guilty [or: more indebted] than all the people dwelling in Jerusalem?

translation_notes: ואני (אני): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'and I' is the obvious reading as the speaker identifies himself.

אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H409 'not', H410 'strength/mighty/God', H411 'these/those', H412 'these/those', H413 'near/to'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect תיראו = 'do not fear', a standard prohibitive construction.

ואחר (first): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'the hind part / after', H311 'after', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 — 'and after [that]' introduces what follows the killing of the body.
אין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/not', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 — 'there is not to them' = 'they have nothing'.
להם: The Strong's candidate H3859 'to rankle' makes no sense here. הם candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — ל + הם = 'to them', a standard dative construction.
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 — 'a thing other' = 'another thing that they can do'.
אחר (second): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H312 — 'other/another', modifying דבר to mean 'another thing'.
שמנה: H8083 'eight'. Only meaningful candidate for a numeral context — combined with עשר to form 'eighteen'.
עשר: Candidates: H6235 'ten', H6236 'ten (Aramaic)', H6237 'to tithe', H6238 'to grow rich', H6239 'wealth', H6240 '-teen'. Chose H6240 because שמנה עשר = 'eighteen', the compound numeral form.

אשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 — relative pronoun 'who/upon whom', connecting to the tower incident.
נפל: Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 'to fall (Aramaic)', H5309 'an abortion'. Chose H5307 — 'fell' describes the tower collapsing upon them.
המגדל: H4026 'a tower'. The other candidates under גדל (H1431–H1435) relate to growing/greatness/tassels, none fitting. With ה prefix = 'the tower'.
והרג: Candidates: H2026 'to smite with deadly intent', H2027 'slaughter'. Chose H2026 — the verb 'and killed' them.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'above/over/against', H5922 same (Aramaic), H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 — comparative use 'over/more than' all the people.
כל: H3605 'the whole/all'. Standard usage — 'all the people'.
textual_notes: בשיבסי — This appears to be a transliteration of a place name (Siloam/Shiloach). No Strong's candidates provided. The spelling differs from the standard biblical שלח (Shiloach, H7975), suggesting a dialectal or later Hebrew rendering.
הגוף — H1479 means 'to hollow/arch/shut', but in later Hebrew גוף means 'body'. This appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew usage for 'body' not captured in the biblical Strong's lexicon.
שיעשו — The only candidate H3299 is the name 'Jaasu'. This is clearly ש + imperfect of עשה ('to do/make') = 'that they can do'. The Strong's entry is irrelevant here.
This section appears to combine material about fearing God rather than men with the incident of the tower in Siloam, suggesting a composite textual unit.

verses.literal: And I say to you beloved do not fear from those who kill the body and after there is not to them [a] thing other that they can do Those eighteen on whom fell the tower in Shiloam and killed them do you think that they were guilty more than all the people dwelling in Jerusalem

verses.translation: But I will teach you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after the death of a person [or: human being], has [the] power [or: strength, authority] to cast [or: send] into Gehenna. And for this [reason] I say to you — fear Him! I say to you: if you do not turn back [or: repent], you will perish [or: be lost] like them.

translation_notes: אבל: Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet'. Chose H61 because it functions as an adversative conjunction 'but/however', contrasting the previous warning about fearing men with the instruction about whom to truly fear.
אני (all instances): H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship'. Chose H589 — the speaker refers to himself throughout.
ממי: H4310 'who?'. With prefix מ = 'from whom', introducing the question of whom to fear.
שאחרי: H317 'other' is listed but here ש + אחרי functions as 'that after', a temporal subordinate clause. The consonants אחרי clearly mean 'after' in this context.
מות: Candidates: H4191 'to die', H4192 'title of song', H4193 'death (Aramaic)', H4194 'death'. Chose H4194 — the noun 'death' fits 'after the death of the person'.

האדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 — 'the human being/person', with definite article ה, referring generically to a person after death.
יש: H3426 'there is'. Only candidate. 'There is to him' = 'he has'.
כח: H3581 'vigor/force/power'. Only candidate. 'Power to send into Gehenna'.
ולזה (זה): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — ו + ל + זה = 'and for this [reason]'.
שאם (אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 — ש + אם = 'that if', introducing a conditional clause.
לא: H3808 'not' vs H3809 same (Aramaic). Chose H3808 — simple negation 'if not you return'.
textual_notes: כא%לו — The % mark appears to be a scribal or manuscript artifact. Reading as כאלו = 'like them/like those'. Could also be read as כאילו 'as if', but 'like them' (referring back to the eighteen killed by the tower) makes better contextual sense as a warning.
אומ%ר — The % mark again appears to be a manuscript artifact. Reading as אומר = 'say'.
לשולחו — infinitive of שלח with ל prefix and 3ms suffix: 'to send him'. The referent of 'him' is the person whose body has died.
בגיהנם — not a biblical Hebrew word with a Strong's number. This is the post-biblical Hebrew form of Gehenna (from גי הנם, the Valley of Hinnom).

verses.literal: But I will teach you from whom you shall fear fear him who after [the] death of the person there is to him power to send him into Gehenna and for this I say to you him fear I say to you that if not you return you will be lost like them

verses.translation: That they [are] sold for a small coin's [or: meager] value, and [yet] not one of them is forgotten before God [the Mighty One].

translation_notes: שהם: Candidates: H7718 'beryl gem', H7719 'Shoham', H1992 'they'. Parse as ש (relative particle) + הם (they) = 'that they'. This fits the clause structure.

שלו: Candidates: H7958 'quail', H7959 'security', H7960 'fault', H7961 'tranquil/careless'. However, in context this likely reads as a possessive 'his/of him' (של + ו). Given the narrative about sparrows being sold, 'of his' or simply a possessive particle makes sense.

במעה: Candidates: H4577/H4578/H4579 'bowels/belly/interior'. However, מעה is also a known small coin (not in Strong's but attested in Mishnaic Hebrew). In context of buying/selling, 'for a small coin' is the coherent reading.
האל: Candidates: H408/H410/H411/H413. With definite article ה, H410 'God/Mighty One' = 'the God' is the only reading that makes sense before whom things are not forgotten.
textual_notes: שלו could be parsed as של+ו (possessive 'his') or as one of the Strong's candidates (quail, security, etc.). 'Quail' would produce 'quails are sold' which is contextually possible but less likely given the overall passage about God's care for small creatures.
במעה — Strong's only lists 'bowels/belly' meanings, but the consonants מעה also represent a small coin in later Hebrew. The commercial context (sold, valuations) strongly supports 'coin'.
ערכין — not in provided candidates; appears to be a plural of ערך (valuation/assessment), fitting the mercantile context.
נמכרין — the ין ending is an Aramaic-style masculine plural participle ending, indicating this text has Aramaic linguistic features.

verses.literal: That they of his [are] sold for a small-coin valuations and one from them not [is] forgotten before the God

verses.translation: And the hairs of your [heads] — all of them are counted [and known]. Do not fear, for you are worth [or: equal in value to] more than many sparrows [or: many who have passed by].

translation_notes: אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God', H413 'to'. Before תיראו (you shall fear), H408 'do not' is the standard prohibitive construction.
אתם: Listed candidate H864 'Etham (place)'. But consonants אתם are universally the 2nd person plural pronoun 'you'. The Strong's listing is incomplete — this is clearly 'you (plural)'.
שוים: Listed candidates are for ים (sea/spring). But שוים is from שוה (to be equal/worth), with plural participle ending. 'You are worth' fits the comparative sentence with יותר.
יותר: H3148 'redundant, more, over and above'. Fits as comparative adverb 'more'.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'for/because'. Standard causal conjunction.
textual_notes: שעברו — 'that passed by/away'. This could refer to sparrows (implied from previous context) or could mean 'many who have gone before'. The verb עבר means to pass over/through/away.
שוים could theoretically involve שו + ים but the participial form of שוה (to be equal/worth) is by far the most coherent reading in a comparative sentence.

verses.literal: And [the] hairs of your [heads] all of them [are] counted to you do not fear for you [are] worth more than many [that] passed away

verses.translation: And I say that every person who acknowledges [or: confesses] me before people, he will be honored [or: called precious] from the heavens [or: by the Heavenly One] before the angels [or: messengers] before God.

translation_notes: ואני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. 'And I say' is coherent; 'and a ship says' is not.
אומר: H201 'Omar (name)' is listed but the consonants אמר with participial form אומר = 'saying/say' from H559. The participle is the standard form.
כי: H3588 conjunction 'that' introducing the content of what is said.
האדם: H120 'human being' with article. In context 'every person' is the clear reading.
בי: H994 'oh that/if it please' — but in context שמודה בי = 'who confesses in me', where בי is simply ב + י (preposition 'in' + 'me').
מן: H4480 'from/out of'. Before ה<מים (heavens), 'from the heavens' fits.
האל: H410 'God/Mighty One' with article. The theological context demands this reading.
textual_notes: ה<מים — the < indicates a damaged or uncertain letter. The likely reconstruction is השמים (the heavens/skies). The missing consonant is probably ש.

יקרהו — could be parsed as יקר + הו (he will be honored/made precious) or יקרה + ו (it will happen to him, from קרה). 'He will be honored' fits better with the heavenly/angelic context; 'it will happen to him from the heavens' is also possible.
בי as a preposition+pronoun 'in me' vs. H994 interjection 'oh please' — the confessional context strongly favors 'in me'.

verses.literal: And I say that every the human who confesses in me before the people he will be honored from the heavens before the messengers before the God

verses.translation: And every person who speaks a word against the Son of Man — it will be forgiven him. But whoever curses [or: reviles] the Spirit of Holiness [the Holy Spirit], it will not be forgiven him.

translation_notes: אדם: H120 'human being'. The generic sense 'any person' fits with כל (every).
דבר: Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. As a noun following שיאמר (who will say), H1697 'a word' is the coherent object.
כנגד: Candidates from נגד: H5046 'to declare', H5048 'opposite/against', H5049 'opposite'. With כ prefix, כנגד = 'against/opposite to'. H5048 fits — speaking a word against someone.
בן: H1121 'son'. Before האדם, this forms 'son of the human/man' — a well-known Semitic title.
האדם: H120 'the human/man'. With article, part of the title בן האדם.
והוא: H1931 'he/it'. Introduces the consequence clause.
רוח: H7307 'spirit/wind/breath'. Before הקדש, 'spirit of holiness' is the clear reading.
הקדש: H6944 'holiness/sacred thing'. With article, 'the holiness' = the Holy [Spirit].
לא: H3808 absolute negation 'not'.
textual_notes: נמחל / ימחלו — the root מחל (to forgive) is post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew, not classical biblical Hebrew (which uses סלח). This confirms the text's later Hebrew register.
ימחלו — 3rd person plural 'they will forgive' used as an impersonal passive: 'it will not be forgiven to him'.

verses.literal: And every human who will say a word against [the] son of the human and he [is] forgiven to him [but] whoever curses [the] spirit of the holiness not they will forgive to him

verses.translation: And when they bring [or: lead] you into synagogues [houses of assembly] and before rabbis [or: authorities] and before prophets [or: rulers], do not be anxious [or: desire] to strive [or: deliberate] about in what manner or in what matter [or: word] you will answer or what you will say.

translation_notes: וכאשר: ו + כ + אשר. H834 'who/which/when'. With כ prefix = 'and when'.
אל: H408 prohibitive 'do not'. Before תחפצו (you will desire), this is the standard negative command.
באי: H335 'where/which'. באי זו = 'in which' — an interrogative construction.
זו: H2097/H2098 'this/that'. Feminine demonstrative matching אופן (manner) in the phrase 'in which manner'.
אופן: H212 'a wheel'. But אופן in Mishnaic Hebrew means 'manner/way' (derived from the wheel concept). Context of 'in which manner you will answer' confirms this semantic development.
זה: H2088 'this/that'. Masculine demonstrative, paired with דבר (word/matter).
דבר: H1697 'word/matter/thing'. 'In which matter/word you will answer.'
או: H176 'or'. Connecting alternative clauses.
textual_notes: אופן — Strong's H212 gives 'wheel' but the word developed into 'manner/way' in post-biblical Hebrew. The context absolutely demands 'manner'.
ולרבנים ולנביאים — 'rabbis and prophets' is unusual. Could refer to religious authorities and civil rulers, or to actual rabbis and prophets. The term רבנים is distinctly post-biblical.
תחפצו — from חפץ (to delight in, desire). Here used in the negative = 'do not desire/be anxious to strive'.

verses.literal: And when they lead you in houses of assemblies and to rabbis and to prophets do not desire to endeavor in which manner or in which thing you will answer or you will say

verses.translation: For the Spirit of Holiness [the Holy Spirit] will teach you in that very hour [or: moment] a response [or: answer] of speech [or: tongue]. Five loaves of my bread are sold for a hundred, and the hairs of your heads — all of them are counted. Therefore, [do not] fear [or: you will see].

translation_notes: כי: H3588 causal conjunction 'for/because'.
רוח: H7307 'spirit'. Before הקדש = 'spirit of holiness'.
הקדש: H6944 'holiness/sacred'.
שעה: Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/look', H8160 'a moment/look'. H8160 'hour/moment' fits with באותה (in that) = 'in that hour'.
מענה: Candidates: H4617 'a reply', H4618 'a furrow'. A reply/answer fits after being taught by the Spirit what to say.
לשון: H3956 'tongue/speech'. 'An answer of tongue' = a spoken response.
שלי: H7987 'privacy'. But שלי in post-biblical Hebrew is simply the possessive 'my/mine' (של + י). Context of 'five loaves of mine' or 'my bread' fits.
במאה: H3967 'a hundred'. 'For a hundred' — a price.
כלם: H3637 'to wound/insult' is listed but כלם here = כל + ם (all of them), from H3605. Standard usage.
לכן: ל + כן. H3651 'so/thus' with prefix = 'therefore'.
textual_notes: This section appears to contain material from two different passages merged together. The first part (Spirit teaching an answer) and the second part (five loaves sold, hairs counted) seem to be from different contexts. This may be a scribal conflation or a marginal gloss that entered the text.
חמשהלחם — compressed writing of חמשה + לחם = 'five bread/loaves'. Unusual placement after the Spirit teaching section.
ושערותראשיכם / ושערותראשכם — two variant forms of 'hairs of your heads' written consecutively, likely representing scribal variants (one with yod suffix, one without). This is a doublet.

תראו — could be from ראה (to see) or ירא (to fear). 'Therefore you will see' or 'therefore fear [not]'. In context of reassurance about God's care, both work but 'do not fear' (connecting to earlier אל תיראו) may be intended despite the positive form here.

verses.literal: For [the] spirit of the holiness will teach you in that hour an answer of tongue five the bread of my [privacy] are sold for a hundred and [the] hairs of your heads and [the] hairs of your heads all of them [are] counted therefore you will see

verses.translation: And one from the group [or: company] said to him, Rabbi, tell my brother that he should divide with me the inheritance.

translation_notes: ואחד: H259 'one'. 'And one from...'
מן: H4480 'from/out of'. Partitive use.
החבורה: H2250 'bound with stripes/weal'. However, חבורה in post-biblical Hebrew means 'company/group/fellowship'. The context of someone from a group speaking demands 'company/group'.
אמר: H559 'to say'. Standard narrative verb.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God', H413 'to'. Before אחי (my brother), H413 'to' is the correct preposition — 'say to my brother'.
אחי: Candidates: H277/H278 proper names. But אחי = אח + י (my brother), from the common noun אח (brother, not separately listed). Context of inheritance dispute confirms 'my brother'.
textual_notes: הירו<ה — the < indicates a damaged/uncertain letter. The likely reconstruction is הירושה (the inheritance), with the missing letter being ש. This fits the context of a brother being asked to divide property.
החבורה — Strong's H2250 means 'stripe/wound' but the same consonants in Mishnaic Hebrew mean 'group/fellowship'. The social context requires 'group'.

verses.literal: And one from the company said to him Rabbi say to my brother that he divide with me the inheritance

verses.translation: And Yeshua said to the man, Who appointed [or: placed] me [as] a judge or a divider over you?

translation_notes: אל: H413 'to'. Before האדם, 'said to the man'.
האדם: H120 'human/man'. The specific man who asked the question.
מי: H4310 'who?' Interrogative pronoun opening the question.

שמני: Candidates listed: H4507 'Fate idol', H4508 'Minni (province)', H5204 'lamentation'. However, the correct parse is ש + מנ + ני: 'who appointed me' — ש (relative/who) + root שׂים/מנה (to appoint/place) + ני (me suffix). The verb מנה (to appoint) or שׂם (to place) with 1cs suffix = 'appointed me'.
textual_notes: שמני — parsing is crucial. Could be: (1) ש + שׂם + ני = 'who placed me' (from שׂם, to place); (2) ש + מנה + ני = 'who appointed me' (from מנה, to appoint). Both produce the same essential meaning. The Strong's candidates listed (H4507, H4508, H5204) do not apply here.
עליכם — 'over you (plural)'. Yeshua addresses the questioner but uses plural, possibly including the brother in the dispute.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said to the human who placed me [as] judge or divider over you

verses.translation: And he said to them, Guard yourselves [or: beware] from all covetousness [or: stinginess], for the life of a person is not [determined] by the abundance of what he possesses [or: holds onto].

translation_notes: ואמר: H559 'to say'. Narrative past 'and he said'.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1992 'they'. Parse as ל + הם = 'to them'. Standard indirect object.
מכל: מ + כל. H3605 'all/every'. 'From all' — introducing what to beware of.
כי: H3588 causal 'for/because'.
חיי: H2425 'to live/life'. Construct form 'life of' before האדם.
האדם: H120 'the human/person'. 'Life of the person.'
מה: H4100 'what'. Introducing relative clause 'what he holds'.
textual_notes: ה<מרו — damaged letter. Likely הִשָּׁמרו (guard yourselves, from שמר) or הִזָּהרו (be warned, from זהר). The imperative 'beware/guard yourselves' fits with the warning about covetousness. The missing letter is probably ש (השמרו).

כילות — not in provided Strong's candidates. The consonants כיל relate to כילי (stingy/miserly) in post-biblical Hebrew. Could also be כליות (kidneys, from כליה) but 'stinginess/covetousness' fits the moral warning.
בהשפעת — post-biblical Hebrew term meaning 'in the abundance/influence of'. Not found in biblical Strong's. From root שפע (abundance/overflow).
<הוא — damaged first letter. Likely שהוא (that he) = ש + הוא, forming the relative clause 'what he possesses'.
מחזיק — from חזק (to seize/hold/be strong). Hiphil participle = 'one who holds/possesses'.

verses.literal: And he said to them beware from all stinginess for [the] life of the human is not in the abundance of what he holds

verses.translation: And he spoke to them a parable [or: illustrative story]: A certain man's field was yielding fruits [or: produce] in great [or: overwhelming] abundance.

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'he said' introducing speech fits the narrative context of telling a parable.
להם (הם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 because ל + הם = 'to them,' the standard prepositional phrase for addressing an audience.

משל: Candidates: H4910 'to rule', H4911 'to use figurative language', H4912 'a pithy maxim/parable', H4913 'Mashal (place)', H4914 'a satire', H4915 'empire'. Chose H4912 because 'a parable' is what is being spoken to an audience, and the narrative that follows is clearly an illustrative story.
שדה: Candidates: H7704 'a field', H7705 'a wife'. Chose H7704 because the context describes produce/fruits growing, which fits 'field' perfectly.

אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'a red gem'. Chose H120 because 'a man's field' producing fruits is the natural subject of this parable.

verses.literal: And he said to them a parable: [the] field of a man was producing fruits in [the] greatness of abundance.

verses.translation: And the man was deliberating [or: reasoning] within himself, saying: What shall I do, since I have no [place] in which to gather [or: store] my good things and my produce?

translation_notes: והאדם (אדם): Candidates: H119 'rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'red gem'. Chose H120 because 'the man' continues the parable subject from section 1.
אומר: The candidate listed is H201 'Omar, a grandson of Esau,' but the consonants אמר are clearly the participle of H559 'to say.' The form אומר is the active participle 'saying.' Assigned to H559.

שאין (אין): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. The prefix ש functions as 'that/because.' Chose H369 because 'for there is not' expresses the man's lack of storage space.
במה: Candidates: H1116 'an elevation', H1117 'Bamah (place)', H4100 'what?'. Chose H4100 with prefix ב: 'in what' = 'with what/wherein,' expressing the man's question about storage capacity.
textual_notes: במה could be read as H1116 'high place' (a single word) or as ב + מה 'in what.' Context of the man asking about storage strongly favors ב + מה.

verses.literal: And the man [was] thinking in himself saying: What will I do, for there is not to me in what I will gather my goods and my fruits?

verses.translation: And he said: I will do this — I will demolish [or: tear down] my storehouses and make them larger [or: more spacious], and I will gather in all the yield [or: products] of my harvest and my good things.

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Chose H559 'to say' for the same reason as section 1 — introducing direct speech.

דברי: The candidate listed is H1704 'Dibri, an Israelite,' but the consonants דבר are the common noun H1697 'word/thing/matter' in construct form. Contextually 'things of my produce' makes sense; the man is talking about gathering all the products of his yield.
textual_notes: תולדותי — from the root ילד/תולדות meaning 'generations/produce/what is brought forth.' Here it likely means the produce/yield of his land rather than genealogical generations.
דברי could be 'words of' or 'things/matters of.' In this agricultural context, 'things/products of' fits better.

verses.literal: And he said: I will do this — I will tear down my storehouses and I will make them more great, and I will gather all [the] things of my produce and my goods.

verses.translation: And I will say to my soul [or: my life-breath]: Great [or: abundant] good things you have stored up for many years — eat [or: feast] and drink and take your rest [or: be at ease].

translation_notes: ואומר: The listed candidate H201 is 'Omar (proper name).' But the consonants are clearly the participle/cohortative of אמר H559 'to say,' with waw prefix: 'and I will say.' Assigned H559.

שנים: Candidate H8147 'two/twofold.' However, the consonants שנים also represent the plural of שנה 'year' (H8141). In context 'for many years' makes far more sense than 'for two.' The plural of שנה shares these consonants.

ושתי: Candidates: H2060 'Vashti (queen)', H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp in weaving.' The consonants שתי here are the imperative/infinitive of שתה 'to drink.' H8358 'intoxication' relates to drinking. Chose this reading because the sequence eat-drink-rest is the natural triad of self-indulgence.
textual_notes: שנים — the consonants could be H8147 'two' or the plural of שנה 'year' (H8141). Context of 'abundance for many years' strongly favors 'years.'

The imperative forms אכלי, ושתי, ותנוחי appear to carry a first-person suffix or feminine singular imperative. Since the soul (נפש) is being addressed and נפש is grammatically feminine, these are likely feminine singular imperatives: 'eat! drink! rest!'

verses.literal: And I will say to my soul: abundance of goods you have gathered for many years — eat and drink and rest.

verses.translation: But God [or: the Mighty One] said to that fool [or: senseless one]: On this very night they will demand [or: require] your soul [or: breath-of-life], and those things that you have prepared — to whom will they belong?

translation_notes: והאל (אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H409 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H411 'these/those', H412 'these/those', H413 'to/near.' With the definite article ה, 'the Mighty One/God' (H410) is the natural reading — God is speaking in judgment to the fool.
אמר: Chose H559 'to say' — God speaks to the fool.
סכל: Candidates: H5528 'to be silly', H5529 'silliness/dolts', H5530 'silly/fool.' Chose H5530 as the adjective/noun 'fool' — God addresses the man as a fool.

בזה: Candidates for בזה: H959 'to disesteem', H960 'scorned', H961 'booty.' For ב + זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that.' Chose ב + H2088: 'in this [night]' — the preposition ב + demonstrative 'this' introducing 'the night' creates the phrase 'on this night.'
textual_notes: בזה could theoretically be the verb H959 'to despise/disesteem' but that would leave הלילה syntactically stranded. Reading as ב + זה 'in this' + הלילה 'the night' produces 'on this night,' which is coherent.
יבקשו — 'they will seek/require.' The impersonal plural 'they will require' is a common way of expressing a divine passive: 'your soul will be required.'

verses.literal: And the Mighty One said to that fool: In this the night they will require your breath-of-life, and those things that you have prepared — from whom will they be?

verses.translation: So [or: thus] is the one who stores up his fruits [or: produce] in this world, yet is not rich toward [or: in] YHWH [the Eternal One].

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/just', H3652 'so', H3653 'a stand/pedestal', H3654 'a gnat.' Chose H3651 because 'so/thus' introduces the moral conclusion of the parable.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be/exist', H1934 'to exist.' Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'he [is]' — the subject of the concluding statement.
הזה: Candidates: H1957 'to dream', or ה + H2088 'this.' Chose the article ה + H2088 'this' because 'this world' (העולם הזה) is a standard phrase.
האוצר: H214 'a depository/storehouse.' With the article, this functions as a participle: 'the one who stores up.'

verses.literal: So is he the [one] storing his fruits in the world the this, and he is not rich in YHWH.

verses.translation: And he said to his disciples: Do not be anxious [or: striving] to seek [or: search out] food for your lives [or: souls], and do not say 'With what shall we clothe our bodies?'

translation_notes: אל (first): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near.' Chose H408 because אל + imperfect verb = negative command 'do not.'
לבקש: Candidates: H1245 'to search out/seek', H7179 'straw.' Chose H1245 because 'to seek food' is coherent; 'to straw' is nonsensical in context.
ואל (second): Same as first אל — H408, forming the second negative command 'and do not say.'
במה: Candidates: H1116 'an elevation', H1117 'Bamah (place)', H4100 'what?'. Chose ב + H4100 'in what/with what' — the question 'with what shall we clothe ourselves?' is the natural continuation.

verses.literal: And he said to his disciples: Do not be striving to seek food for your souls, and do not say in what you will clothe your bodies.

verses.translation: For the soul [or: life] is more precious [or: valuable] than food [or: eating], and the body [is worth] more than clothing [or: garments].

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that.' Chose H3588 as the conjunction 'for/because,' introducing the reason for the preceding instruction.
הנפש: Candidates: H5314 'to breathe/be refreshed', H5315 'a breathing creature/soul/life.' Chose H5315 — 'the soul/life' is the subject being compared.
והגוף: H1479 'to hollow/arch/close.' The consonants גוף in later Hebrew mean 'body.' Context clearly requires 'body' as the parallel to 'soul' and contrasted with 'clothing.'
מהלבוש: H3830/H3831 'a garment.' With prefix מ = 'than clothing.' Chose H3830.
textual_notes: ח(שובה — the parenthetical mark in the consonants suggests a textual note or uncertain letter. The root חשב means 'to think/reckon/esteem,' and חשובה would mean 'esteemed/important/precious.' This fits perfectly: the soul is more precious than food.
מא(כילה — similarly has a parenthetical mark. The root אכל 'to eat' in hiphil/nominal form = 'food/eating.' The מ prefix = 'than.'

verses.literal: For the soul [is] important more than food, and the body [is] more than clothing.

verses.translation: Consider [or: reflect upon] the ravens — they do not sow and do not glean [or: harvest], and they have no storehouses and no granaries, yet YHWH [the Eternal] feeds them. As it is written: 'Who prepares for the raven his food [or: provision]?' How much more are you worth than they!

translation_notes: ולא (both): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not.' Chose H3808 as the standard Hebrew negation particle.
ואין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?' Chose H369 — 'and there is not' negates the possession of storehouses.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'them.' Chose H1992 with ל prefix: 'to them' = they have.
ויהוה: H3068/H3069. Chose H3068 — the divine name YHWH as the subject who feeds the ravens.
יכין: Listed as H3199 'Jakin (proper name).' But the consonants כון in hiphil imperfect = 'he prepares/provides' (from H3559). This is a quotation from Job 38:41. The verb means 'prepares/provides.'
כמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', or כ + H4100 'how/what.' Chose כ + H4100 = 'how much' — introducing the comparative exclamation.
מהם: ם + H1992 'them' with prefix מ = 'than them' — the comparative 'more than them.'
textual_notes: יכין — the Strong's candidate given is H3199 'Jakin (proper name),' but in context this is clearly the hiphil imperfect of כון (H3559) meaning 'to prepare/provide,' quoting Job 38:41.
שוים — from the root שוה 'to be equal/worth.' The ים suffix here is the masculine plural participle ending: 'you are worth.' Not related to H3220 'sea.'
The quotation mark (') after צידו indicates the end of a scriptural citation (Job 38:41).

verses.literal: Think on the ravens, that they do not sow and do not glean, and there is not to them storehouses and not granaries, and YHWH feeds them, as it is written: Who prepares for the raven his provision? How much you are worth more than them.

verses.translation: Who among you, by deliberating [or: worrying], is able to add a single cubit [or: forearm's length] to his stature [or: span of life]?

translation_notes: יוכל: The candidate H3116 is 'Jukal (proper name).' However, the consonants יכל represent the imperfect of H3201 'to be able/prevail.' In context 'who is able' is clearly the intended reading.

לחשוב: The candidate H2815 is 'Chashshub (proper name).' However, the consonants חשב represent the infinitive of H2803 'to think/reckon/devise.' Context: 'to think/worry' — by anxious thought, who can add to his stature?

אמה: Candidates: H519 'a maidservant', H520 'a cubit (forearm measure)', H521 'cubit', H522 'Ammah (place)', H523 'a community', H524 'a community.' Chose H520 because a cubit is a unit of physical measurement, fitting the image of adding to one's stature.
textual_notes: קומה can mean 'stature/height' or metaphorically 'lifespan.' Both readings are coherent: adding a cubit to one's physical height, or adding a measure to one's life. The Hebrew leaves this genuinely ambiguous.

verses.literal: Who among you is able to think [that] he will add to his stature a cubit?

verses.translation: And if this small [or: least] matter is not in your hands to do, why [or: for what reason] do you strive with diligence [or: earnestness] concerning the rest of the matters?

translation_notes: ואם (אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this is clearly a conditional clause introducing a logical argument.

הדבר (דבר): Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'matter/thing' fits the context of something one might or might not be able to do.

המעט (מעט): Candidates: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little/small', H4593 'sharp', H5842 'stylus'. Chose H4592 because 'the small [thing]' modifies the matter as an adjective, producing a coherent image of a small task.
הזה (זה): Candidates: H1957 'to dream', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as the demonstrative pronoun 'this' naturally modifies 'the small matter'.
על (first): H5921 'upon/concerning' chosen because it introduces the object of striving.
יתר: Candidates: H3498 'to exceed/remain', H3499 'remainder/rest', H3500 'Jether'. Chose H3499 because 'the rest of the matters' contrasts logically with 'this small matter'.
textual_notes: תשתדלו is a hitpael-like form not in the standard biblical lexicon; it appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew verb from the root שדל meaning 'to strive/endeavor'. No Strong's number available.
בח(ריצות appears to be a noun form meaning 'diligence/earnestness' from the root חרץ (H2742 'sharp/diligent'); the parenthetical marking suggests textual uncertainty in the manuscript.
לע(שות: The parenthetical mark suggests possible manuscript damage; the reading עשה (to do/make) is contextually clear.

verses.literal: And if the matter the small this there-is-not in-your-hands to-do, upon what will-you-strive with-diligence upon the-rest-of the-matters?

verses.translation: Consider the lilies [or: bulb-flowers] of the field — how they grow! They do not toil and they do not spin. I say to you that Solomon in all his grandeur [or: exaltation] did not have a garment resembling [or: comparable to] the garment of one of these.
words: (fragmentary letter, possibly end of previous word)

translation_notes: השדה (שדה): Candidates: H7704 'field', H7705 'wife/mistress'. Chose H7704 because 'lilies of the field' produces a coherent natural image; 'lilies of the wife' does not.

שלמה: Candidates: H8008 'a dress', H8009 'Salmah', H8010 'Solomon', H8011 'retribution'. Chose H8010 because the passage compares royal splendor to flowers, and Solomon is the iconic figure of wealth and glory — 'in all his greatness not having a garment' is coherent with Solomon as subject.
מלבוש: Candidates: H4403 'garment/clothing', H3830 'garment', H954 'to be ashamed'. Chose H4403 as the full form מלבוש meaning 'garment' fits the clothing imagery perfectly.

דומה: Candidates: H1745 'silence/death', H1746 'Dumah (place)'. Neither fits well as a dictionary entry; however the consonants דמה also map to the root meaning 'to resemble/be like' (H1819/H1820). In context, 'resembling' is the only reading that makes sense — 'garment of silence' or 'garment of Dumah' produce incoherent images.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' is coherent; 'a ship says to you' is not.
textual_notes: ת at the beginning appears to be a fragmentary consonant — possibly the end of a word from a previous section or a damaged portion of the manuscript. It could be the imperative ending or a relative particle.

ח(בצלות: The parenthetical mark suggests textual uncertainty. The reading likely derives from בצל (H1211 'onion/bulb'), with the form meaning 'bulb-flowers' or 'lilies'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew form.

דומה: The Strong's candidates H1745/H1746 do not fit; the word is almost certainly from the root דמה 'to resemble' (H1819), used here as a participle 'resembling'. The provided candidates may be incomplete.
מעלתו: Likely from the root עלה (H4609 or H4608) meaning 'elevation/ascent/greatness', with 3ms possessive suffix. No exact Strong's match for this noun form was provided among candidates.
מאלו: 'of these' — the candidates H431 'lo!' and H432 'if' do not fit; this is the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (אלו), a later Hebrew form of אלה.

verses.literal: [Consider] the lilies-of the-field how they-grow not they-toil and-not they-spin I say to-you that Solomon in-all his-greatness not was to-him garment resembling to-the-garment-of one of-these

verses.translation: If so [it is that] the grass which is in the field today and tomorrow [is thrown] into the oven — YHWH clothes it — so how much more [and how much more] will he clothe you! Why [are] you [people] of little faith [or: trust, firmness]?

translation_notes: אם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose H518 because 'if so' introduces a conditional/logical conclusion.
כן (first): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'if so' is a standard Hebrew construction.
שהוא (הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 same, H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 — the relative ש + pronoun הוא = 'that it [is]'.
בשדה: Candidates: H7704 'field', H7705 'wife'. Chose H7704 — grass in the field is coherent; grass in the wife is not.

כמה/וכמה: Candidates: H3642 'to pine after', H4100 'what/how much'. Chose H4100 — 'how much and how much' is the Hebrew idiom for 'how much more', which fits the a fortiori argument perfectly. 'Pining' would be contextually bizarre.
במעט: Candidates: H4591 'to lessen', H4592 'a little', H4593 'sharp', H5842 'stylus'. Chose H4592 because 'in little faith' describes deficient trust.
יהוה: Candidates: H3068/H3069. Chose H3068 — the divine name as subject of 'clothes it'.
textual_notes: The phrase כמה וכמה is a post-biblical Hebrew idiom meaning 'how much more' (kal va-chomer reasoning). Each word individually could be parsed as H3642 'to pine' but the idiomatic pairing makes H4100 'how much' the only viable reading.

מלבישו and שמלביש are hiphil participle forms of לבש 'to clothe' — the first with 3ms suffix ('clothes it'), the second as a relative clause ('that he clothes'). These are post-biblical Hebrew morphological forms.

verses.literal: If so the-grass that-it [is] in-the-field the-day and-tomorrow in-the-oven YHWH clothes-it so how-much and-how-much [more] he-clothes you why [are] you in-little faith

verses.translation: And do not desire [or: delight in seeking] to seek out what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not exalt yourselves [or: be anxious, be lifted up] upward [or: to a high place].

translation_notes: ואל (both): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because the construction ואל + imperfect verb is the standard prohibitive in Hebrew — 'do not'.
לבקש: Candidates: H1245 'to search out/seek', H7179 'straw'. Chose H1245 because 'to seek what you will eat' is coherent; 'straw what you will eat' is not.

למעלה: Candidates: H4608 'elevation/acclivity', H4609 'elevation/ascent', H5927 'to ascend', etc. Chose H4608 — 'to a height' or 'upward', fitting with the verb 'lift yourselves up'. The phrase תתנשאו למעלה means 'exalt yourselves upward' or idiomatically 'be haughty/anxious'.
textual_notes: תתנשאו is a hitpael form of נשא 'to lift/carry'. It could mean 'exalt yourselves' (be haughty) or 'be carried away' (be anxious/worried). In context, following prohibitions against anxious seeking of food and drink, the sense may be 'do not be anxious' or 'do not be lifted up [in worry]' rather than 'do not be arrogant'. Both readings are plausible.
תחפצו appears to be from חפץ (H2654 'to delight in, desire'). No Strong's candidates were provided for this word.

verses.literal: And do-not desire to-seek what you-will-eat and-what you-will-drink and-do-not lift-yourselves-up to-height

verses.translation: For all these matters the creatures of the world [or: the nations of the age] seek after, and your Father knows in truth [or: with certainty] that you have need [or: deficiency] of all these things.

translation_notes: האלה (אלה): Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. None of these standard entries match; however אלה is also the common Hebrew demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not always assigned a Strong's number separately). In context, 'all the matters these' = 'all these matters' is the only coherent reading.
אלה (final): Same analysis as above — demonstrative 'these' is the only reading that fits 'from all these'.
כי (both): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 — 'for' and 'that' are standard uses of this conjunction.
textual_notes: נבראי appears to be a construct plural of נברא (niphal participle of ברא H1254 'to create'), meaning 'created ones of'. This is a post-biblical Hebrew form not in the standard Strong's lexicon.
שואלים could be from שאל (H7592 'to ask/inquire') — 'ask for/seek'. No candidates were provided but the root is clear from consonants.
האלה and אלה: The Strong's candidates listed are all unrelated to the demonstrative pronoun 'these'; the demonstrative אלה (sometimes listed under H428) is clearly intended.

verses.literal: For all the-matters the-these ask-for [the] created-ones-of the-world and-your-father knows in-truth that to-you [there is] deficiency from-all these

verses.translation: Indeed [or: verily], seek the kingdom [or: dominion] of YHWH, and all these matters you will attain [or: overtake, obtain].

translation_notes: אמנם: Candidates: H551 'verily', H552 'verily'. Both are identical in meaning; chose H551.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'a rule/dominion', H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah'. Chose H4438 because 'kingdom of YHWH' is coherent; 'Cuthah of YHWH' is meaningless.
אלה: Same as section 5 — demonstrative 'these'.
textual_notes: תשאלו is an imperfect 2mp from שאל (H7592 'to ask/seek'). It could be indicative ('you will seek') or jussive/imperative in force ('seek!'). Given the adverb אמנם 'indeed' and the overall hortatory context, an imperative sense is most likely.
תשיגו is from נשג/השיג (H5381 hiphil 'to reach, overtake, attain'). No candidates were provided but the root is clear.

verses.literal: Indeed seek the-kingdom-of YHWH and-all these the-matters you-will-attain

verses.translation: Do not be fearful [or: afraid] of a weak [or: frail] nation [or: flock], for it is pleasing [or: agreeable] to your Father to give to you [a] kingdom [or: dominion].

translation_notes: אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God', H411 'these', H413 'to'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect = prohibitive 'do not'.
מגוי (גוי): H1471 'nation/troop of animals'. The only candidate; 'from a nation' fits with 'weak'.
חלש: Candidates: H2522 'to prostrate/overthrow', H2523 'frail/weak'. Chose H2523 as an adjective modifying 'nation' — 'a weak nation'. A verb 'to prostrate' would not fit syntactically after a noun.

ערב: Candidates: H6148 'to braid/traffic/pledge', H6149 'to be agreeable/pleasing', H6150 'to grow dusky', H6151 'to commingle', H6152 'Arabia', H6153 'dusk'. Chose H6149 because 'it is pleasing to your Father to give you a kingdom' produces the most natural image — the Father delights in giving. 'Evening' or 'Arabia' or 'to pledge' produce incoherent sentences.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'kingdom', H3575 'Cuthah'. Chose H4438 — 'kingdom' completes the sentence coherently.
textual_notes: מגוי חלש: 'from a weak nation' is unusual. This could mean 'because of a weak/small flock' if גוי is taken in its secondary sense of 'a troop of animals' (H1471 includes this meaning). The address to a 'small flock' told not to fear would cohere well with the reassurance that follows. Both 'nation' and 'flock' readings are viable.
תת is the construct infinitive of נתן (H5414 'to give'). No candidates were listed but the form is standard.
יראים could be from ירא (H3372/H3373 'to fear/fearful'). No candidates listed but the consonants and context are unambiguous.

verses.literal: Do-not be fearing from-a-nation weak for to-your-father [it is] pleasing to-give to-you [a] kingdom

verses.translation: Sell what you are holding [or: possessing] and give charity [or: righteousness, beneficence], for you [are] preparing [or: establishing] a treasure [or: storehouse] in the heavens [where] there is no deficiency, where no thief approaches it and [where] a moth does not consume [it].

translation_notes: צדקה: Candidates: H6665 'beneficence', H6666 'righteousness/justice/virtue'. Chose H6666 as the broader term encompassing charity/righteousness — both meanings apply in context of giving after selling.
אוצר: H214 'depository/treasure'. Only candidate; fits perfectly as the treasure being prepared.
שגנב (גנב): Candidates: H1589 'to thieve', H1590 'a stealer/thief'. Chose H1590 — 'that a thief' as a noun subject is more natural than the infinitive here.

מכלה (כלה): Candidates: H4357 'completion', H3615 'to end/consume/destroy', H3616 'pining', H3617 'destruction', H3618 'bride'. Chose H3615 because 'moth does not consume' is a coherent physical image of moth damage to stored goods.
ועש: H6211 'a moth'. Only candidate; moths consuming garments/treasure is a standard image.
textual_notes: כ י appears to be כי split across a line or word break in the manuscript. Reading as the conjunction כי (H3588) 'for/because'.

<אתם and ב<מים: The angle bracket < likely indicates manuscript damage or an editorial mark. <אתם is 'you (pl.)' and ב<מים is almost certainly בשמים 'in the heavens' (from שמים H8064), with some consonants obscured.
למי שגנב: This could be parsed as 'to the place where a thief' or 'for whomever steals'. The construction למי ש- in post-biblical Hebrew means 'where/to whom that'. Both yield similar meaning.
מתקנים: From the root תקן (H8626 'to straighten/set in order'). This is a post-biblical Hebrew participial form meaning 'preparing/establishing'.
אינה: Feminine form of אין 'there is not' — agreeing with עש (moth) taken as feminine, or possibly with a feminine implied subject.

verses.literal: Sell what you hold and-give righteousness for you [are] preparing treasure in-heaven [where] there-is-no deficiency where thief does-not approach to-it and-moth does-not consume

verses.translation: And in the place where your treasure will be, there your heart will be — wholly [or: completely] united [or: as one]. [Fragmentary:] And if so...

translation_notes: שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name/reputation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name'. Chose H8033 because 'there will be your heart' completes the locative construction 'in the place where... there...'.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify/collect thoughts', H259 'one/united/first'. Chose H259 because 'your heart complete, one' = undivided/wholly focused — a coherent spiritual image.
ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose H518 — 'and if' beginning a new conditional clause.
textual_notes: א׳ is an abbreviation (indicated by the geresh mark ׳). It could stand for אמן 'amen', אחר 'another/after', or another word. Without more context, this is unresolvable.
א״כ is a standard abbreviation for אם כן 'if so'. The double geresh (״) confirms this is an abbreviation rather than a word.
שלימה: This appears to be the feminine adjective form of שלם 'complete/whole/perfect' (related to H8003). It modifies either 'heart' (לבב is sometimes treated as feminine) or serves adverbially.
The end of this section appears fragmentary or transitional — the abbreviations and incomplete clause suggest either manuscript damage or a scribal shorthand.

verses.literal: And-in-the-place that-will-be your-treasure there will-be your-heart complete one ... and-if ...

verses.translation: Let your loins be girded [or: belted, bound up] and [let] burning lamps [or: torches, flames] be in your hands.

textual_notes: מתניכם: From מתנים (H4975 'loins/hips'), with 2mp possessive suffix. Standard Hebrew but no candidates were provided.
חגורים: From חגר (H2296 'to gird/bind'), masculine plural passive participle — 'girded'. No candidates provided.
ועשישות: Likely from עשישה/עששית — a lamp or torch (related to H6251 or post-biblical עששית 'lamp'). The ה-less feminine plural form suggests 'lamps/torches'. This is a rare or post-biblical term.
דולקות: From דלק (H1814 'to burn/kindle'), feminine plural participle — 'burning', agreeing with the feminine עשישות.

verses.literal: Your-loins girded let-them-be and-lamps burning in-your-hands

verses.translation: And you shall be like people who are expectantly waiting for their master when he returns from the wedding celebration, so that when he arrives and knocks [or: strikes] at the door, they will open for him at once [or: from hand, immediately]

translation_notes: מן (MN): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from', H4482 'musical chord'. Chose H4480 because 'from the wedding' is the only coherent reading with the verb 'returns'.
כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: that/when/because'. Chose H3588 because a conjunction is required after למען to form the purpose clause.

ויגע (WYGʿ): Candidates: H3021 'to gasp/be exhausted/toil', H3022 'earnings', H3023 'tired'. The consonants י-ג-ע here in post-biblical Hebrew carry the sense of 'touch/strike/knock'. In context with 'at the door', knocking is the only coherent image — not exhaustion or earnings.
מיד (MYD): From H3027 'hand' — the prepositional phrase מיד means 'from [the] hand', i.e. immediately/at once.
textual_notes: המחכים: The root חכה (to wait/expect) is not listed in the candidates; only H2445 חכים (wise/Magian) appears. The participial form 'the ones waiting' fits the context perfectly (people waiting for their master), while 'wise men/Magians' would not cohere with the parable structure. This likely reflects a root not captured in the provided Strong's entries.

ויגע: Standard biblical Hebrew יגע means 'to toil/be weary', but in post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew נגע can mean 'to touch/knock'. The context 'at the door' demands 'knock'. This may reflect a later Hebrew usage not perfectly captured by the biblical lexicon entries provided.

verses.literal: And be like men [who are] waiting [for] their master when he returns from the wedding feast so that when he comes and knocks on the door they will open for him immediately

verses.translation: And at once he will bless [or: pronounce blessed] them — they [are] the servants who are found awake [or: watchful] when their master comes. In truth I say to you, he will seat [himself] and cause them to recline [at table], and he will serve them

translation_notes: הם (HM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because 'they are the servants' forms a coherent emphatic identification.
אני (ʾNY): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' is a coherent speech formula; 'a ship says to you' is nonsensical.

אומר (ʾWMR): The candidate provided is H201 'Omar (proper name)'. However, these consonants are clearly the participle of אמר (H559) 'to say'. The form אומר is the active participle 'saying/one who says'. Assigning H559.
בבוא (BBWʾ): H935 with prefix ב — 'at the coming of', an infinitive construct with preposition.
textual_notes: ומיד יברכם: 'Immediately he will bless them' — the subject of 'bless' is ambiguous; contextually it refers to the master blessing the watchful servants.

וישרתם: Could be parsed as 'and he will serve them' (3ms + 3mp suffix) or 'and they will serve him' — but the radical reversal of master serving servants is the point of the parable, so 'he will serve them' is the more striking and contextually coherent reading.

verses.literal: And immediately he will bless them they [are] the servants the ones found awake at the coming of their master in truth I say to you that he will be sitting and will do with them that they recline and he will serve them

verses.translation: And if he comes in the second watch or the third and finds them in this [state], blessed [or: fortunate, radiant] are they — those servants

translation_notes: ואם (WʾM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'and if he comes' forms a conditional clause, which is the only coherent reading.

במשמר (BMŠMR): Candidates: H4929 'guard/watch (the post or period)', H8104 'to guard', H8105 'wine sediment', H8106 'Shemer', H8107 'observance'. Chose H4929 because 'in the watch' (night watch period) fits perfectly with the temporal context of second or third watch.
שני (ŠNY): Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'second', H5204 'lamentation'. Chose H8145 because 'second watch' is the obvious temporal reference.
כן (KN): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because 'finds them thus' (i.e., in this manner, still watching) is the coherent reading.
הם (HM): Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 — 'they are the servants' is a predication.
ההם (HHM): The article ה + H1992 הם = 'those' (demonstrative), referring to 'those servants'.
textual_notes: מאו<רים: The consonants appear damaged (indicated by angle bracket). The likely reading is מאושרים (blessed/fortunate) from אשר, or possibly מאורים (illuminated/radiant) from אור. Context — describing the state of the faithful servants — supports either 'blessed' or 'radiant'. I read it as 'blessed/fortunate' since it parallels the blessing in section 2.

verses.literal: And if he comes in [the] second watch or third and finds them thus blessed they [are] the servants the those

verses.translation: But know this: that if the master of the house [or: father] had known at which hour the thief was destined to come, he certainly would have stayed awake and would not have allowed [anyone] to dig through [or: break into] his house

translation_notes: אבל (ʾBL): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay/truly/yet' (adversative). Chose H61 because 'but/however' introduces a contrast with the preceding parable, which is the natural discourse function here.
זה (ZH): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this you shall know' is coherent; 'a sheep you shall know' is not.
שאם (Š + ʾM): Candidates for אם: H517 'mother', H518 'if/conditional'. Chose H518 — 'that if the father knew' forms a conditional clause.

האב (HʾB): Candidates: H1 'father', H2 'father (Aramaic)', H3 'green plant', H4 'green plant'. Chose H1 because 'the father/householder' is the subject who would guard against a thief; a green plant would be nonsensical.

באי (BʾY): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because 'in which' (באי זו שעה = 'in which hour') is the interrogative required by context.
זו (ZW): Candidates: H2097 'this/that', H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (month)'. Chose H2097 — the demonstrative/relative 'which' completing 'in which hour'.
שעה (ŠʿH): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a moment/hour'. Chose H8160 because 'hour/moment' fits with 'in which hour the thief comes'.
הגנב (HGNB): Candidates: H1589 'to steal', H1590 'a thief'. Chose H1590 because the article ה marks this as a noun 'the thief', not a verb.
עתיד (ʿTYD): Candidates: H6263 'prepared', H6264 'prepared/future/destined'. Chose H6264 because 'destined/about to come' captures the future intention of the thief.
ולא (WLʾ): Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation.
textual_notes: האב: Literally 'the father' but in this context likely functions as 'the master of the house / householder' (a common usage). The parable compares the householder to someone who should stay vigilant.

אמת שיהיה ניעור: This could be read as 'truly he would have been awake' (apodosis of the conditional) or as an independent assertion 'it is certain that he would have been awake'. The former reading is more natural as the consequence of the 'if he had known' clause.

חפור: This appears to be the infinitive construct of חפר 'to dig', referring to the ancient method of breaking into mud-brick houses by digging through walls. 'Digging through of his house' = 'breaking into his house'.

verses.literal: But this you shall know that if the father knew in which hour the thief [is] about to come truly he would be awake and not allow [the] digging through of his house

verses.translation: And you — stand ready [and] awake, for at the hour that you do not expect [or: reckon, calculate], the Son of Humanity [or: the Human One] will come

translation_notes: כי (KY): Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction'. Chose H3588 because 'for/because' introduces the reason for the command to stay awake.
בשעה (BŠʿH): H8160 'hour/moment' with prefix ב — 'in the hour'. This is the temporal expression matching section 4.
שלא (Š + Lʾ): H3808 'not' with prefix ש (relative particle) — 'that not', forming 'in the hour that you do not expect'.
בן (BN): Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of the human' is a coherent title/designation.

האדם (HʾDM): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'human being/mankind', H121 'Adam (name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'son of the human' (בן האדם) is a recognized designation meaning 'human one / mortal / representative human'.
textual_notes: ואתם: The provided candidate H864 'Etham (place name)' does not fit; this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'and you' (ואתם). No Strong's number applies to the basic pronoun form here in the same way.

בן האדם: Could theoretically be 'son of Adam' (H121) reading it as a proper name, or 'son of the human' (H120) as a generic/titular designation. Context — an eschatological coming figure — supports the titular reading 'the Son of Humanity'.

verses.literal: And you stand awake for in [the] hour that not you reckon it will come [the] son of the human

verses.translation: And Kepha [Peter/the Rock] said to him, Master, are you speaking this matter [or: word, parable] to us, or to everyone?

translation_notes: אמר (ʾMR): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because 'said' as a verb of speech is the only coherent reading.
אדון (ʾDWN): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/master', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because Kepha is addressing his master, not calling him by the name 'Addon'.
זה (ZH): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'this matter/word' is coherent.

הדבר (HDBR): Candidates: H1907 'vizier', H1696 'to speak', H1697 'word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'this word/matter' (i.e., this parable/teaching) is what Kepha is asking about.
לכל (LKL): H3605 'all/every' with prefix ל — 'to all/everyone'.
textual_notes: אמור לנו זה הדבר או לכל: The syntax is ambiguous — it could be an imperative 'Say to us: [is] this matter [for us] or for all?' or it could be a question 'Are you saying this matter to us or to all?' Both yield essentially the same meaning.

verses.literal: And Kepha said to him master say to us this the word or to all

verses.translation: And our master said: Let your loins be girded [or: prepared] and [your] lamps [burning]. For every person [who is] faithful and manages the expenditure [or: distribution] with wisdom — that person the master appoints over his household, to give to the members of his household the grain [or: wheat, provisions] that is fitting to give them at its proper time

translation_notes: אמר (ʾMR): Chose H559 'to say' — speech verb introducing discourse.
לכל (LKL): H3605 with prefix ל — 'for every/to all'. Context requires 'for every person who is faithful'.
האיש (HʾYŠ): H376 'man/person' — 'the man/person who is faithful' is the subject being described.
בחכמה (BḤKMH): Candidates: H2451 'wisdom', H2452 'wisdom (Aramaic)'. Chose H2451 — standard Hebrew 'in wisdom'.

משים (MŚYM): The root שים 'to set/place/appoint'. The candidates listed (H3220 'sea', H3221 'sea', H3222 'warm spring') are for the suffix ים, but here the whole word is a hiphil/qal participle of שים — 'the one who sets/appoints'. The ים suffix candidates are irrelevant.
האדון (HʾDWN): H113 'sovereign/master' — 'the master appoints over his house'.
על (ʿL): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'over/upon', H5922 'over (Aramaic)', H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 — 'over his house' is the natural prepositional usage.

לבני (LBNY): Candidates: H3845 'Libni', H3846 'Libnite', H1137 'Bani', H1138 'Bunni', H5204 'lamentation'. All are proper names or unrelated. This is clearly ל + בני (construct of בנים 'sons') from H1121. 'To the sons of his house' = household members.
להם (LHM): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1992 'they'. This is ל + הם = 'to them'. Chose H1992.
textual_notes: The structure of this verse is complex. It appears to combine two sayings: (1) 'Let your loins be girded and your lamps [burning]' — a command to readiness, and (2) a question or statement about 'who then is the faithful and wise steward whom the master appoints over his household.' The transition between these two parts is abrupt in the Hebrew.
ועששיות: This word (lamps/lanterns) has no Strong's candidate provided. It appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew word for oil lamps or lanterns, from the root עשש.
משים: The candidates listed are for ים (sea/spring), but the word is clearly the participle of שים (to set/appoint). No exact Strong's match is provided for this parsing.
החטה: H2406 'wheat' — this could be literal (wheat rations) or figurative (provisions/sustenance). The parable context suggests provisions/food distribution.

verses.literal: And our master said loins arranged you shall be and lamps to every the man the faithful and doing the expenditure in wisdom that the man sets the master over his house to give to [the] sons of his house the wheat the fitting to give to them in its time

verses.translation: Blessed [or: fortunate, radiant] is that servant whose master finds him doing thus [or: so doing]

translation_notes: הוא (HWʾ): Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. Chose H1931 — the emphatic pronoun 'he is' in a predication 'blessed is he'.

עבד (ʿBD): Candidates: H5647 'to work/serve', H5648 'to do (Aramaic)', H5649 'servant (Aramaic)', H5650 'servant', H5651 'Ebed (name)', H5652 'deed'. Chose H5650 'servant' because the passage is about a servant/steward.

שרבו (ŠRBW): The ש is relative particle 'that/whose', רבו from רב meaning 'his master/great one'. Candidates for רבו: H7238 'increase of dignity', H7239 'myriad', H7240 'myriad (Aramaic)'. The word here means 'his master' — רב as a title of authority. H7238 (dignity/greatness) is closest to this usage.
כן (KN): Candidates: H3651 'thus/so', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'thus doing' means 'doing in this manner / faithfully carrying out his duties'.
textual_notes: מאו<ר: Damaged text (angle bracket). Same word as in section 3. Could be מאושר 'blessed/happy' or מאור 'light/radiant'. Both yield a positive exclamation about the servant. I read 'blessed/fortunate'.
שרבו: Could be parsed as ש + רבו 'that his master' or ש + רב + ו 'that his great-one'. Both yield the same meaning contextually.

verses.literal: Blessed he [is] that servant that his master finds him thus doing

verses.translation: Truly I say to you, over all the things [or: possessions] that he holds [or: has in his charge], he will give him authority [or: cause him to rule]

translation_notes: אני (ʾNY): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — 'I say' is the speech formula.
אומר (ʾWMR): H201 'Omar' is the only listed candidate, but this is clearly the participle of H559 אמר 'to say'. Assigning H559.

שעל (ŠʿL): Candidates: H8168 'palm/handful', or ש + על (H5921 'over/upon'). Chose ש + H5921 because 'that over all the things' is the coherent construction — the relative particle ש plus the preposition על. 'A handful of all the things' does not fit the context of granting authority.
כל (KL): Candidates: H3605 'all/whole', H3606 'all (Aramaic)'. Chose H3605.
textual_notes: שעל: This could theoretically be the single word H8168 שעל 'handful', but parsing as ש + על 'that over' is far more coherent with the following 'all the things that he holds, he will give him rule'.

verses.literal: Truth I say to you that over all the things that he holds he will cause him to rule

verses.translation: But if that servant says in his heart, My master is delaying his coming, and he begins to beat [or: strike] the young servants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and become drunk

translation_notes: אבל (ʾBL): Candidates: H56 'bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H59 'Abel', H60 'lamentation', H61 'but/yet/truly'. Chose H61 because 'but if that servant says' introduces the contrasting negative scenario after the positive one.
אם (ʾM): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/conditional'. Chose H518 — conditional 'if' introducing the hypothetical scenario.
עבד (ʿBD): Candidates: H5647 'to work', H5648 'to do', H5649 'servant (Aram.)', H5650 'servant', H5651 'Ebed', H5652 'deed'. Chose H5650 'servant' — continuing the parable about a servant.
לבוא (LBWʾ): H935 with prefix ל — infinitive 'to come'.

להכות (LHKWT): The candidate H3575 'Cuth/Cuthah' does not fit. This is clearly ל + הכות, the hiphil infinitive construct of נכה 'to strike/beat'. The provided candidate is irrelevant; the form means 'to strike/beat'.
textual_notes: וה<פחות: Damaged text. The likely reading is השפחות 'the maidservants' (from שפחה). The angle bracket indicates textual damage or uncertainty in the consonants.

להכות: The only Strong's candidate provided (H3575 'Cuthah') is a place name and clearly wrong for this context. The word is the hiphil infinitive of נכה (to strike), a common biblical Hebrew verb. No appropriate Strong's entry was provided among the candidates.

verses.literal: But if that servant says in his heart my master delays to come and begins to strike the young men and the maidservants and eats and drinks and becomes drunk

verses.translation: His master [or: lord] will come on a day he does not anticipate [or: await, expect] and at an hour [or: moment] he does not know, and will cast him out to destruction [or: perdition, the place of perishing].

translation_notes: שעה (consonants שעה): Candidates: H8159 'to gaze/inspect', H8160 'a look, a moment'. Chose H8160 because the context pairs it with 'day' as a temporal marker — 'in a day… and in a moment/hour' — making a time-unit reading far more natural than 'gazing'.
textual_notes: אדוניו is not listed in the provided candidates; it is parsed as אדון + 3ms suffix, 'his lord/master'.
יקווהו appears to be a form of קוה (to wait, expect, hope) with 3ms suffix — 'he expects/awaits him'. No candidates were provided.
ידעה could be parsed as ידע + 3fs suffix (he knows her/it) or as 3ms imperfect of ידע. Context suggests 'he does not know [it]' referring to the hour.

verses.literal: His master will come in [a] day that he does not expect him and in [an] hour that he does not know and will drive him out to destruction.

verses.translation: But [or: truly] that servant who knew the desire [or: will, pleasure] of his master and does not ready himself and did not act according to his will — he will be struck [or: beaten] with many plagues [or: afflictions, blows].

translation_notes: אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'a meadow', H59 'Abel (place)', H60 'lamentation', H61 'nay, truly, yet'. Chose H61 because the passage introduces a contrasting case ('but that servant who…'), making the adversative/affirmative particle the natural fit.

עבד (consonants עבד): Candidates: H5647 'to work/serve', H5648 'to do/make', H5649 'a servant', H5650 'a servant', H5651 'Ebed (name)', H5652 'a deed'. Chose H5650 because the context describes 'that servant who knew' — a noun is required.
שידע (consonants ש+ידע): Candidates: H3045 'to know', H3046 'to know (Aramaic)', H3047 'Jada (name)'. Chose H3045 because ש + ידע = 'who knew', a standard Hebrew relative clause.
textual_notes: מוכה is parsed as a passive participle of נכה (to strike/smite) — 'struck/beaten'. The provided candidates under כה (H3541/H3542) are not relevant here; מוכה derives from the root נכה (H5221).
מזמין is a hiphil participle of זמן (to prepare/appoint), a post-biblical Hebrew form not in the standard Strong's list. The meaning 'preparing/readying' fits the context perfectly.
בעליו is parsed as בעל + 3ms suffix, 'his master/owner' (cf. H1167). No candidates were provided.

verses.literal: But that servant who knew [the] will of his master and does not prepare himself and did not do according to his will, will be struck [with] many plagues.

verses.translation: And the one who did not recognize [or: know, discern] and did things deserving [of punishment] will be struck with few plagues [or: afflictions]. And a person to whom much [or: a great thing] is given — much [or: a great thing] will be required of him. And the one to whom they have entrusted [or: deposited with] an abundant matter — an abundant matter will be demanded of him.

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because the context discusses 'a person to whom much is given' — a generic human referent.

verses.amplified: And he said to the crowds: When you see a cloud rising from [or: facing toward] the west, immediately you say 'Rain is coming!' — and the rain comes.
work: ואומר (consonants אמר): No Strong's candidates provided for the root אמר directly, but this is clearly a form of the common verb 'to say' (H559). The candidate H201 'Omar' (a proper name) makes no sense in context with a prefix ו and the following speech discourse. Read as 'and he said.'

כאשר (כ + אשר): Candidates include H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher'. With כ prefix and followed by a verb תראו ('you see'), the conjunction 'when' (H834) is the only reading that produces a coherent clause: 'when you see.'

ענן: Candidates: H6049 'to practice magic', H6050/H6051 'a cloud', H6052 'Anan (a name)'. In context — something you 'see' rising toward the west that predicts rain — 'cloud' (H6051) is the only coherent reading.

נגד: Candidates: H5046 'to front/manifest/declare', H5047 'to flow', H5048 'a front/opposite/toward', H5049 'opposite'. Following a noun (ענן) and preceding a directional noun (מערב), the adverbial/prepositional sense 'opposite/facing toward' (H5048) fits naturally: 'a cloud facing the west.'

מערב: Candidates: H4627 'traffic/mercantile goods', H4628 'the west'. A cloud facing toward 'mercantile goods' is incoherent; a cloud facing toward 'the west' makes perfect meteorological sense — western clouds bring rain from the Mediterranean. Chose H4628.

מיד (מ + יד): From H3027 'hand'. The prepositional phrase מיד literally means 'from hand' and idiomatically means 'immediately/at once.' This fits the context perfectly: upon seeing the cloud, they immediately speak.
המטר (both occurrences): Candidates: H4305 'to rain' (verb), H4306 'rain' (noun). With the definite article ה prefix, this must be a noun — 'the rain' (H4306).
ambiguities: The verb form ואומר could theoretically be parsed as a participle ('and [one] saying') or as a prefix conjugation with waw ('and he said/says'). Context of direct speech to crowds suggests a narrative introduction, likely completed action 'and he said.'

נגד מערב could be read as 'opposite the west' (i.e., facing westward) or 'from the direction of the west' depending on how one construes the spatial relationship. Both yield the same essential meaning: a cloud associated with the western direction.
